notes: Home page for the South African site. Seven blocks as fixed in CONTENT-SCHEMA.md, each 60 words or fewer including labels, one call to action per block and two in closing. Hero: the brief's positioning line and a subline that says what FHS does from South Africa, with no region beyond that because regions served are unknown. Hero secondary is omitted on purpose: one button per screen; the urgent action stays in the header. Ask: the five doors in nav order, one line naming who each door is for, and the brief's urgency band per door. The urgency value describes how quickly that visitor usually needs an answer (the brief's doors table); the component should label it as such, for example 'Typical timescale', and never present it as a response time, because none has been agreed. How: the brief's five steps condensed, using the brief's own words per step; the About page carries the full version. Trust: four things a visitor can check now (verification, process, group, company details) with a single link to the commitments on About; item hrefs are left out to keep one action per block. Engine360: 'is being designed' is the headline; the text names only status and exposure, as far as the brief goes. Group: the fixed group line as title; the Swiss company is described from the Swiss site's content and labelled as the Swiss company; the relationship word (subsidiary, sister or partner) is not rendered until confirmed; the link goes to the Swiss site so the visitor can check it. Closing: primary plus urgent, per the fixed labels. Nothing on this page states an address, phone, region, engine or aircraft type, approval, team member, client name, response time or year count. British English, no dashes as punctuation.
